extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains. These sentences have been translated into 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process to enable better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia. A third of the sentences were collected from Wikinews, a third from Wikijunior, and a third from WikiVoyage. An article was selected at random from each source, and then a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences were manually selected from each article.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia (specifically Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Segments with very short or malformed sentences were avoided. To avoid bias coming from the document structure, one paragraph per document was carefully selected from either the beginning, middle, or end of the article, balanced to be equally distributed across the whole corpus.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each target language, sentences are translated by a translation Language Service Provider (LSP). The resulting translations are automatically checked. If these checks fail, translations are sent back for re-translation. If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation. If the quality is not sufficient, translations are sent back to the original translation LSP for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality is assessed through a Translation Quality Score on a 0 to 100 scale, determined by the number of identified errors (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register). Each error is associated with a severity level (minor, major, critical). The acceptable translation quality score threshold was set to 90%.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The sentence selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in the lab (6 male, 4 female) with different roles (researchers, scientists, engineers, program/project managers) originally coming from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America. Translations and evaluations were performed by professional translators from Language Service Providers.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks included language identification, checking if the translation is a copy of the source sentence, checking for significantly different length, checking translation fluency according to a language model, and checking if the translation is a copy from publicly available translation engines using sentence-level SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dev and devtest splits are publicly downloadable. The test set will not be released but will be available via a publicly available evaluation server to guarantee equivalent assessment and reduce overfitting. The authors hope to continue to expand the number of languages covered.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in the machine translation community for low-resource languages, which are spoken by the majority of the world's population, allowing them to benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: To avoid bias from document structure, paragraph locations were balanced across the corpus. To avoid translation bias, automatic checks were implemented to detect and reject professional translations that were likely copies from commercial translation engines.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Source sentences not in English are produced by human translators, which may introduce translationese (overly literal or awkward translations) with known idiosyncrasies, though the authors conjecture these effects are marginal when evaluating models in low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. Use cases include evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems, document-level translation, multimodal translation, and text classification. Usage Guidelines: The dev set is meant for hyper-parameter tuning. The devtest is meant for testing during the development phase. The test set is available via a public evaluation server.
